claim: Raptor already played Bench Boost in GW1 and it went very well, scoring 192 points and ranking 38k overall.
quote: I of course went for bench boost one. That's gone very well. I've had back-to-back successful weeks, 192 points so far, up to 38k overall rank.

claim: Raptor is playing Triple Captain this GW3 and expects it to stick.
quote: we played the bench boost in game week one, the triple captain is active for game week three, and I'm pretty sure it will stick

claim: Raptor is triple-captaining Haaland this week and feels good about it.
quote: I love the triple captainship. I want to play it this week on Erling Haaland. I feel good about it

claim: Raptor is now leaning about 80% towards playing his Wildcard in GW4 rather than GW3 or a GW4 Free Hit, driven by new injuries in his squad.

claim: Raptor plans to save his Free Hit for a strong-looking week between GW9 and GW12, or to hold in reserve for a postponement-driven double gameweek.

claim: Raptor's player referred to as Hinchcliffe (also captioned Hinshwood/Hincheywood elsewhere, likely Hinshelwood of Brighton) is injured and expected out until the international break.

claim: Rodon is injured and expected to miss this gameweek and be out until the international break, disrupting Raptor's plan to use him as a nailed cheap Leeds defender.

claim: Raptor is worried about Ballard's minutes this week away at a strong Brentford side and does not plan to start him.
quote: Ballard I genuinely worry about his minutes. Brentford are brilliant and it's away. So, I don't want to play Ballard.

claim: Raptor calls Calafiori brilliant and starts him as a core defender this week.
quote: I've got Calafiori who's brilliant, Ajer who I think is a great cheap player.

claim: Raptor rates Ajer as a great cheap defender and may still keep him even after wildcarding in GW4.
quote: Ajer who I think is a great cheap player. I may even still have Ajer on my wildcard in four.

claim: Raptor keeps Maguire this week despite doubts about a Man Utd clean sheet, citing his attacking threat and defensive contribution upside.
quote: Maguire's not perfect, but he does have attacking threat. We've seen it time and time again. He could get defcon in a game like Everton.

claim: Raptor thinks Gomes is a really nice underrated asset and is happy to keep starting him.
quote: I actually think Gomes is a really nice underrated asset. Again, I think Leeds are pretty solid defensively, but I'm happy to have him.

claim: Raptor's player captioned as Solanke/Solis (Arsenal midfielder, per known caption mangling this is Tzolis) is the biggest concern in his team after a poor, nearly-sent-off Gameweek 2 following a strong Gameweek 1.
quote: the only player that majorly concerns me in my own team for this week is Solanke... In Gameweek 2, it was horror. His output was horrid.

claim: Raptor thinks there is a real chance Eze starts instead of the player captioned Solis/Solanke (Tzolis) in the London derby against Chelsea, though he is not certain.

claim: Raptor is happy to keep Bruno Fernandes this week, citing good underlying data beyond just his return in GW2.
quote: Fernandes and Mbeumo I have no issue playing this week. Not just because they returned in two, but the data they're putting up is very good.

claim: Raptor is happy to keep Mbeumo this week, citing strong underlying data and takes in-swinging set pieces.
quote: a City mid could outscore Bryan Mbeumo, but the guy's getting a lot of chances, takes in-swinging set pieces, and I think Everton are there to get at

claim: Raptor is starting João Pedro despite a tough away trip to Arsenal, citing Chelsea's excellent attacking form.
quote: Joao Pedro though and Chelsea are in exceptional attacking form. I don't think Arsenal are completely like immune from conceding chances and goals.

claim: Raptor starts Calvert-Lewin despite a clash with his own goalkeeper's fixture, noting he is on penalties and plays 90 minutes.
quote: Calvert-Lewin's fine. He's on penalties and he plays 90.

claim: Raptor is leaning towards starting Kinsky over Verbruggen this week to reduce a clash with his own Leeds/Brighton attackers, noting Spurs conceded very little xG in GW2.
quote: playing Kinski over Verbruggen would actually reduce a clash... I might end up starting Kinski

claim: Raptor likes Anderson as a transfer target if he sells his struggling Arsenal midfielder, citing set-piece duty and defensive contribution upside against a Coventry side that must focus on marking City's bigger names.
quote: I think he's fine. I don't think he has super high upside, but I also like him for this week.

claim: Raptor is also considering Schade as a target this week, saying his data has always been great and he could have more upside than Anderson at home to Sunderland.
quote: Schade's data has always been great... Does Schade have more upside than Elia Anderson? You could argue yes.

claim: Raptor predicts Foden starts alongside Cherki this week rather than being dropped for Ndiaye, and considers a double-move to bring him in.

claim: Raptor likes Groß this week as a target, citing penalties, set pieces and a home fixture.
quote: Hinchcliffe to Pascal Groß, and I actually really like Groß this week... Pascal Groß on penalties, on set pieces, with a home fixture, feels decent

claim: Raptor lists Man City rotation as a key uncertainty this week: whether En-Nesyri and Enzo go straight in, whether Cherki and Foden both get reduced minutes, whether Foden even starts, and whether Gvardiol and Nico Williams both start.
quote: Do En-Nesyri and Enzo go straight back in? Do Cherki and Foden both get reduced minutes? Does Foden even start? Do Gvardiol and Nico Williams both start

claim: Fantasy Football Hub's AI transfer tool recommends Raptor upgrade his Hinchcliffe-type player to Szoboszlai this week, but Raptor is not convinced it's worth two transfers before a wildcard.
quote: they recommend that I do Mbeumo to Anderson and Hinshwood to Szoboszlai... I don't know. I'm just not that convinced.

claim: Raptor's final plan is to triple-captain Haaland, wildcard in GW4, and make one transfer now selling his Arsenal midfielder (captioned Solanke) for either Anderson or Schade, keeping a transfer to roll.

claim: Raptor flags an issue named Sol Bamba (unresolved against the roster) alongside his Hinchcliffe and Rodon injury concerns.
quote: On top of that, Sol Bamba looks like an issue.

claim: Harry confirms he is not playing his Wildcard in GW3 and is likely to play Triple Captain instead this week.
quote: I am not playing my wildcard this week... I'm likely going to play the triple captain chip, but if I was, that's the draft I would go with.

claim: Harry is weighing three transfer options this week, most involving selling Bruno Fernandes to Cherki, though he notes keeping Bruno also has a case now that Man Utd won big.
quote: I sell Bruno to Cherki, I sell Bryan and Benmo to Cherki, or I don't buy Cherki. And I still think that I will sell one of the Man United duo

claim: Harry's main midfield target this week is Cherki, funded by selling one of his Man Utd midfielders.
quote: Doing Bryan and Benmo to Cherki, I'm sure you're all saying, 'Harry, that's just the obvious move.'

claim: Harry is planning ahead to buy Cole Palmer in GW4 for Hull at home, which affects whether he sells Bruno or Mbeumo this week.
quote: Bruno is going to have to leave my team if I want to buy Palmer in Gameweek 4 for Hull at home.

claim: Harry notes Man Utd's 5-1 win over Ipswich (Bruno hat-trick and assist, Mbeumo goal and assist) has caused panic about selling their players, but cautions it was against an easy Ipswich side.
quote: Bruno Fernandes getting a hat-trick and an assist, Bryan Mbeumo an assist and a goal. And suddenly, there's lots of panic

claim: Harry rates Newcastle top for fixtures over the next 6 weeks and highlights their attackers and cheap defenders as wildcard targets.
quote: Newcastle are right at the top. So, some of their attackers like Yoane Wissa, Alanger, or some of their cheaper defenders like Malick Tchouameni, Lewis Hall, or Djed Spence

claim: Harry says Arsenal and Chelsea have great fixtures from GW4 onward, though the two teams play each other in GW3 which is a headache for whether to start their assets.
quote: from Gameweek 4 onwards, they have fantastic fixtures, but they play each other in Gameweek 3, which does feel like a pretty difficult game to call

claim: Harry rates Man Utd's upcoming fixtures far down the list, which is why owners of Bruno or Mbeumo should be considering taking them out on wildcard.
quote: Man United are far down there. And that is why if you've got a Bruno or an Mbemba, you probably are considering taking them out on wildcard.

claim: Harry rates Brighton, Bournemouth, Leeds and Sunderland poorly for fixtures, suggesting owners of Sunderland picks like Ballard consider moving on.

claim: Calafiori is a core pick in Harry's example wildcard draft as part of a triple-up on the Arsenal defense.
quote: I've gone with a triple up on the Arsenal defense. I've gone with David Raya in goal. I've gone with Calafiori.

claim: Harry warns not to start Konsa until he is confirmed as a starter, watching for his price drop and whether he plays Monday night against Aston Villa.
quote: Don't put Konsa in your FPL team until he drops in price... So, I wouldn't start him against Chelsea.

claim: Harry benches Egan for defensive-contribution value in his draft but doesn't expect Hull's defense to remain this strong all season.

claim: Harry prefers Gibbs-White over Mbeumo in his draft, citing set pieces, penalties, no European football and safe minutes.

claim: Harry keeps Szoboszlai in his draft for cheap, consistent defensive-contribution points, calling him a safe pick alongside minutes-risk players like Cherki.

claim: Harry starts Sangaré ahead of João Pedro in his draft, calling him a great pick for defensive contributions.

claim: Haaland starts up front in Harry's wildcard draft as an obvious pick at home to Coventry.

claim: Harry prefers Wissa over Calvert-Lewin in his draft for Newcastle's stronger long-term fixtures.

claim: Harry is unsure whether Guéhi or Dias will be the one to drop out of the Man City back line and left them out of his draft as a result.

claim: Harry expects Gvardiol (captioned Vardyol) to likely play center-back if Enzo Fernandez's arrival pushes O'Reilly to left-back, which would squeeze Guéhi or Dias out.

claim: Harry names Martinez of Chelsea as his preferred goalkeeper if downgrading from Raya, citing very good long-term Chelsea fixtures from GW4.

claim: Harry shows a stretch wildcard draft where Bruno Fernandes, Palmer and Haaland can all be squeezed in together via downgrades elsewhere, but advises against actually doing it.

claim: Harry suggests Cherki could later be sold on to Morgan Rogers once his fixtures turn or minutes become an issue.
